chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: Enjoyment and no resentment among sidemen
summary: He says no one resented him and the men stayed with him.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well, especially playing trumpet the way you were playing it, I mean then to be able to pick up a trombone and a sax and all those instruments.
It gave me a little trouble.
That's right. It weren't, I just, oh, at that age where I was then I just enjoyed myself with it.
Yeah, that seems to be pretty much what I get from our whole talk. You enjoyed yourself.
I did. I really did. I enjoyed myself through those years. You know, by me being able to do this and do that, it made it better for me, you know?
And the, and the thing about the boys, the enjoyed seeing me doing it. They felt good about it and had fun. They enjoyed seeing me do it. And we'd just kid each other about this or that.
We used to go out about one, two o'clock in the afternoon and rehearse until
about 5. Then, we'd have to come back to work at 9.
Yeah. Quite often, we run into the fact that sometimes people resent, or they're envious, other that people get things that they would like to have for themselves.
That's right.
Have you had instances where this has been made known to you? That some of the sidemen wished they were in a position to do more of what you did rather than what they did?
No, not in my band.
Not in your band.

No. I didn't have no trouble there. We'd just laugh and go along with that. You know, cause, I'll tell you the truth. If I thought that maybe one of them resented, I wouldn't bother cause I wouldn't want to hurt him. I really wouldn't want to have nobody feeling that way towards me. I wouldn't bother.

Yeah, but it also sounds like you went out of your way to be sure that they were getting their too. I mean, you made it a point to see that they were all getting showcased and doing the solos and things like that.
Right.
I mean, as you said before, you saw to it that they were able to demonstrate what they could do.
Right. That's the way that I felt.

I don't know how well you paid them or anything like that. But, if they didn't go anyplace, you must have been paying them enough. I mean, if they stayed there for 15 years and things like that, the implications are that at least they had to be somewhat satisfied.
Yeah. I took care of them.
Yeah, that's what I was saying. So, the implication would be that
they would have to be, you know, somewhat satisfied.
That's true.

You can't force people to have that kind of family feeling. You can't force people. You can't even make them slaves. You know, you have to do it in any kind of way whether through economics or anything else, and make it work. And, you did it and Duke did it.
Right. That's right.
The guys just stayed right there with Duke too.
Well, I never had any trouble with those fellows. And what I went through with them, and they were great. I'll never regret it. I have no regrets.
Yeah.

They were beautiful men. And, (inaudible) the was even that came in later years cause I didn't want to be bothering nobody, you know. That wasn't right. If I thought I was gonna have trouble with someone, I just wouldn't
bother.
